metadata.title: Union Army of the Potomac -- Brigade Level Order of Battle
sources: Busey, John W. and Martin, David G. -- Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg (Longstreet House, 1994)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Gottfried, Bradley M. -- Brigades of Gettysburg (Da Capo Press, 2002)
metadata.notes: All 49 Union infantry brigades plus cavalry brigades. Each brigade record includes commander, regiment_ids list, strength, casualties, and days engaged.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, First Corps (Iron Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Solomon Meredith
commander.fate: Wounded July 1 -- concussion from horse fall under fire

brigades.key_action: Charged into Herbst Woods July 1 morning -- broke Archer's Confederate brigade and captured General Archer himself. Iron Brigade black hats recognized by Confederates: 'That's no militia -- that's the Army of the Potomac.'

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, First Corps (Cutler's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: North of Chambersburg Pike -- initially pushed back by Davis; 6th Wisconsin charge at Railroad Cut saved the brigade's position.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, First Corps (Paul's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Gabriel Paul
commander.fate: Wounded July 1 -- shot through both eyes, blinded permanently

successor.name: Colonel Richard Coulter
successor.assumed_command: July 1 -- fourth commander in one afternoon

brigades.key_action: Oak Ridge defense. Paul blinded, then three successive commanders wounded in under an hour. 16th Maine left as sacrifice regiment to cover retreat.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, First Corps (Baxter's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Delivered the stone-wall ambush that destroyed Iverson's Confederate brigade at Oak Ridge -- Iverson's Pits.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Third Division, First Corps (Biddle's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: South of Chambersburg Pike -- Seminary Ridge fighting. Three brigade commanders wounded in succession.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Third Division, First Corps (Stone's Bucktails)
brigades.key_action: Bucktail Brigade astride Chambersburg Pike. 149th PA suffered 84% casualties -- one of the highest single-regiment rates of the battle.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Third Division, First Corps (Stannard's Vermont Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Decisive flanking maneuver July 3 -- wheeled left to enfilade Kemper's brigade, then 16th VT wheeled again against Wilcox. Double enfilade that helped seal Pickett's repulse.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Second Corps (Cross's Brigade)

commander.name: Colonel Edward Cross
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- shot through abdomen in the Wheatfield. Hancock told him 'This is not your last fight Cross.' Cross replied 'I think this IS my last battle.'

brigades.key_action: Wheatfield -- Cross killed almost immediately upon entering the field.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Second Corps (Irish Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Father Corby's general absolution on the knoll before charging into the Wheatfield. Brigade reduced to 532 men from 4,000+ at the war's start.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, First Division, Second Corps (Zook's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Samuel Zook
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- mortally wounded in the Wheatfield

brigades.key_action: Wheatfield -- Zook killed.

brigades.designation: Fourth Brigade, First Division, Second Corps (Brooke's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Pushed farthest into the Wheatfield of any Union brigade on July 2.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Second Corps (Harrow's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: 1st Minnesota's sacrifice charge July 2 -- 85.5% casualties in 15 minutes buying time for Hancock.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Second Corps (Webb's Philadelphia Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Held the stone wall at The Angle -- the precise focal point of Pickett's Charge. Cushing's battery was immediately behind their line.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Second Division, Second Corps (Hall's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Cemetery Ridge -- Devereux led 19th MA to reinforce Webb at The Angle without orders during Pickett's Charge.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Third Division, Second Corps (Carroll's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Counterattacked to drive Louisiana Tigers off Cemetery Hill July 2 evening. 8th Ohio in advanced position enfiladed Brockenbrough's brigade during Pickett's Charge.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Third Division, Second Corps (Smyth's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Cemetery Ridge -- delivered close-range fire on Pettigrew's division July 3.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Third Division, Second Corps (Willard's Brigade)

commander.name: Colonel George Willard
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- killed by artillery shell while commanding brigade charge

brigades.key_action: Harper's Ferry regiments seeking redemption -- charged Barksdale's exhausted Confederates near Plum Run. Willard killed. Sherrill later mortally wounded July 3.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Third Corps (Ward's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Devil's Den and Triangular Field -- Ward's brigade held the rocky ground south of Little Round Top.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Third Corps (DeTrobriand's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Rose Woods and Wheatfield -- DeTrobriand's line anchored the Union position in the Wheatfield area.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, First Division, Third Corps (Graham's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Peach Orchard salient -- bore the full force of Barksdale's charge. Graham captured.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Third Corps (Carr's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Emmitsburg Road fighting withdrawal to Cemetery Ridge.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Third Corps (Excelsior Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Excelsior Brigade -- Emmitsburg Road retreat.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Second Division, Third Corps (Burling's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Most regiments detached from brigade control before battle -- 5NJ, 6NJ, 7NJ, 8NJ served under Humphreys directly. Burling left with only 2NH and 115PA.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Fifth Corps (Tilton's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Stony Hill -- Tilton's controversial withdrawal exposed DeTrobriand's flank.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Fifth Corps (Sweitzer's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Rose Woods and Wheatfield -- Sweitzer's brigade bore heavy losses.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, First Division, Fifth Corps (Vincent's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Little Round Top -- arrived just in time. Vincent mortally wounded. 20th Maine's bayonet charge on the left. Rice assumed command.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Fifth Corps (Day's Regular Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Regular Army brigade -- Wheatfield area.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Fifth Corps (Burbank's Regular Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Wheatfield -- Regular Army brigade suffered 41.6% casualties.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Second Division, Fifth Corps (Weed's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Stephen Weed
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- shot on Little Round Top summit beside Hazlett

brigades.key_action: Little Round Top summit -- Weed and Hazlett killed side by side. O'Rorke's 140th NY charged downhill without orders.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Third Division, Fifth Corps (McCandless's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Crawford's charge down Little Round Top's western slope July 2 evening -- drove Wofford's Confederates back through the Wheatfield.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Third Division, Fifth Corps (Fisher's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Big Round Top -- occupied the summit July 2 evening with minimal opposition.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Eleventh Corps (Von Gilsa's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Barlow's Knoll -- struck by Gordon's flank attack on the extreme Union right.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Eleventh Corps (Ames's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Adelbert Ames
commander.fate: Survived -- promoted to division command during battle

brigades.key_action: Barlow's Knoll -- Ames promoted to division command when Barlow fell.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Eleventh Corps (Coster's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Brickyard disaster -- trapped by Hays's Confederates from three sides north of Gettysburg.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Eleventh Corps (Smith's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Cemetery Hill reserve -- lighter casualties than most XI Corps brigades.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Third Division, Eleventh Corps (Krzyzanowski's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Routed north of town -- Krzyzanowski's largely immigrant brigade caught in the XI Corps collapse.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Third Division, Eleventh Corps (Schimmelfennig's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Alexander Schimmelfennig
commander.fate: Cut off during retreat -- hid in a pigpen in Gettysburg until July 4

brigades.key_action: Retreat through Gettysburg town. Schimmelfennig famously hid in a pigpen to avoid capture -- emerged July 4.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Twelfth Corps (McDougall's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Upper Culp's Hill -- McDougall's brigade held the right of the XII Corps position.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Twelfth Corps (Lockwood's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Lockwood's brigade included the 150th NY -- the single largest infantry regiment at Gettysburg with 765 men. Also included 1st Maryland (Eastern Shore) which fought near 1st Maryland Confederate at Culp's Hill.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, First Division, Twelfth Corps (Colgrove's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Colgrove's controversial charge across open meadow July 3 morning -- 2nd MA's Mudge killed saying 'It is murder but it is the order.'

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps (Candy's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Lower Culp's Hill -- left July 2 evening, returned July 3 to fight to recapture Confederate-occupied works.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps (Kane's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Thomas Kane
commander.fate: Ill during battle -- Cobham temporarily commanded

brigades.key_action: Kane's tiny 714-man brigade held the most exposed section of lower Culp's Hill.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps (Greene's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: LONE STAND on Culp's Hill July 2 evening -- Greene held the entire hill with 1,424 men against Johnson's 6,500 Confederates. One of the finest defensive stands of the war.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, First Division, Cavalry Corps (Gamble's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: McPherson's Ridge dismounted defense July 1 morning -- bought critical time for Reynolds to arrive with I Corps.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, First Division, Cavalry Corps (Devin's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Right flank screen July 1 -- protected XI Corps' right flank as long as possible.

brigades.designation: Reserve Brigade, First Division, Cavalry Corps (Merritt's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Reserve brigade -- operations south of battlefield near Emmitsburg Road.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Second Division, Cavalry Corps (McIntosh's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: East Cavalry Field July 3 -- blocked Stuart's attempt to reach Union rear.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Second Division, Cavalry Corps (Huey's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Gregg's division -- east of battlefield.

brigades.designation: Third Brigade, Second Division, Cavalry Corps (Custer's Michigan Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General George Armstrong Custer
commander.notes: Custer had just been promoted to brigadier general. He personally led the mounted charge shouting 'Come on, you Wolverines!'

brigades.key_action: East Cavalry Field July 3 -- Custer's mounted charge stopped Stuart's attempt to reach the Union rear during Pickett's Charge.

brigades.designation: First Brigade, Third Division, Cavalry Corps (Farnsworth's Brigade)

commander.name: Brigadier General Elon Farnsworth
commander.fate: KIA July 3 -- killed in Kilpatrick's doomed charge against Confederate infantry. General for only 4 days.
commander.notes: Farnsworth protested the order as suicidal. Kilpatrick insisted. Farnsworth led the charge and was killed.

brigades.key_action: Kilpatrick's doomed charge against Confederate infantry south of Round Tops -- Farnsworth killed.

brigades.designation: Second Brigade, Third Division, Cavalry Corps (Richmond's Brigade)
brigades.key_action: Kilpatrick's division -- small detachments from various regiments.
